topics.label: Propositions & Connectives
topics.summary: Statements with exactly one truth value, combined with ¬, ∧, ∨ and order of operations. The vocabulary for everything that follows.

topics.label: Truth Tables
topics.summary: Systematically test a compound proposition in every possible world; the mechanical check behind equivalence and valid arguments.

topics.label: Conditionals & Biconditionals
topics.summary: p → q, vacuous and trivial truth, converse / inverse / contrapositive, sufficient vs. necessary, and p ↔ q.

topics.label: Logical Equivalence & Laws
topics.summary: Tautologies, contradictions, De Morgan's laws and the algebra of logic: rewrite formulas step by step, labelling every law used.

topics.label: Predicates & Quantifiers
topics.summary: P(x), domains of discourse, ∀ and ∃, free vs. bound variables, witnesses and counterexamples, negating quantified statements.

topics.label: Nested Quantifiers
topics.summary: Quantifier order and scope, translating English with several quantifiers, nested negation and “exactly one” statements.

topics.label: Rules of Inference
topics.summary: Modus ponens, modus tollens, hypothetical syllogism, resolution, and quantified instantiation / generalization for building valid arguments.

topics.label: Direct Proof & Contraposition
topics.summary: Prove p → q by assuming p and deriving q, or by proving ¬q → ¬p. Definitions of even, odd and rational numbers as proof tools.

topics.label: Proof by Contradiction
topics.summary: Assume the negation and derive the impossible: irrationality of √2 and Euclid's infinitude of primes.

topics.label: Cases & Exhaustion
topics.summary: Split the claim into cases that together cover every possibility, or check every instance of a finite claim.

topics.label: Mathematical Induction
topics.summary: Base case + inductive step: the ladder argument for statements about all n ≥ n₀ (sums, inequalities, divisibility).

topics.label: Strong Induction
topics.summary: Assume the claim for every smaller case, e.g. prime factorization. The natural proof tool for recursive definitions.

topics.label: Sets & Set Operations
topics.summary: ∈ vs. ⊆, set-builder notation, power sets, ∪ ∩ − complement, set identities mirrored from the laws of logic.

topics.label: Cartesian Products
topics.summary: Ordered pairs and tuples, A × B and its size; the ground set on which relations and functions live.

topics.label: Relations & Properties
topics.summary: Relations as subsets of A × B, digraph and matrix views, inverse and composition, reflexive / symmetric / antisymmetric / transitive.

topics.label: Closures of Relations
topics.summary: Repair a relation with the fewest added pairs: reflexive r(R), symmetric s(R) and transitive t(R) closures.

topics.label: Modular Arithmetic
topics.summary: a ≡ b (mod m) means equal remainders; the go-to example of an equivalence relation.

topics.label: Equivalence Relations & Partitions
topics.summary: Reflexive + symmetric + transitive relations, equivalence classes, and the correspondence with partitions.

topics.label: Partial & Total Orders
topics.summary: Reflexive, antisymmetric, transitive relations; comparability, total orders, divisibility and ⊆ as running examples.

topics.label: Hasse Diagrams & Extrema
topics.summary: Draw a poset without the redundant edges; maximal / minimal, greatest / least elements, upper and lower bounds.

topics.label: Functions
topics.summary: A relation with exactly one output per input: domain, codomain, range, images and pre-images.

topics.label: Injections, Surjections & Inverses
topics.summary: One-to-one, onto and bijective functions, composition and inverse functions; the language for comparing sizes.

topics.label: Sequences
topics.summary: Functions on the integers: indices and terms, arithmetic, geometric and harmonic sequences.

topics.label: Summations
topics.summary: Σ notation, index shifts, splitting sums, closed forms for arithmetic and geometric series.

topics.label: Recurrence Relations
topics.summary: Define a term from earlier terms plus initial values; modelling growth, Fibonacci, and recursive processes.

topics.label: Solving Recurrences
topics.summary: Unroll with recursion trees (subtract-1 and divide-by-2 patterns), guess a closed form and prove it by substitution / induction.

topics.label: Growth of Functions (O, Ω, Θ)
topics.summary: Eventual upper, lower and tight bounds with witnesses c and n₀; comparing algorithm running times.

topics.label: Product, Sum & Subtraction Rules
topics.summary: The basic counting principles: multiply independent stages, add disjoint cases, subtract overlaps or count the complement.

topics.label: Permutations
topics.summary: Ordered arrangements P(n, r) = n!/(n−r)!, equivalently counting injective functions.

topics.label: Combinations
topics.summary: Unordered selections C(n, r): r-element subsets, where the order of selection is forgotten.

topics.label: Pigeonhole Principle
topics.summary: If more objects than boxes, some box holds two: no injection from a larger set into a smaller one.

topics.label: Binomial Theorem & Pascal
topics.summary: Expanding (x + y)ⁿ with binomial coefficients; Pascal's identity and triangle.

topics.label: Inclusion–Exclusion
topics.summary: Count a union of overlapping sets by alternately adding and subtracting intersections.

topics.label: Graphs
topics.summary: Vertices and edges, degrees, paths, cycles, connectivity, Euler circuits and graph isomorphism.

topics.label: Trees
topics.summary: Connected acyclic graphs, rooted trees and spanning trees.
